Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 108, verses 1–3:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾: That is, indeed the Lord of Might and Majesty has bestowed upon you, O our Prophet, al-Kawthar, that is, a river in Paradise.

﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾: That is, give thanks for that by praying to your Lord, the One who has bestowed favour upon you, alone, and sacrifice to Him alone.

﴿Indeed, your enemy﴾: That is, the one who hates you.

﴿is the one cut off﴾: That is, the most lowly and humiliated, the one whose line of descent is cut off.

The meaning of the verses:

The words of the Most High, ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar. So pray to your Lord and sacrifice. Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾: These three verses are specific to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), for he is the one addressed by them, and they carry the character of consolation to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It is related that when the son of the Prophet (ﷺ), al-Qasim, died, al-As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi said: "Muhammad is cut off" (batar), or "he is cut off" (abtar), meaning he has no offspring after him. So Allah the Most High sent down this surah, containing a rebuttal of al-As, consolation for the Messenger (ﷺ), and good tidings to him and to his Ummah with al-Kawthar, which is a river in Paradise, whose two banks are of gold, whose course is over pearls and rubies, whose soil is more fragrant than musk, whose water is sweeter than honey and whiter than snow. From al-Kawthar fills the Basin (al-hawd) that is in the plains of the Resurrection, and none will be turned away from it except the righteous of his Ummah (ﷺ).

As for the words of the Most High, ﴿Indeed, We have granted you﴾: that is, We have specially favoured you with al-Kawthar, which is a river in Paradise, one of its greatest rivers, along with the abundant good which Allah the Most High has bestowed upon you: prophethood, the true religion, the elevation of your remembrance, and the praiseworthy station.

And the words ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾: that is, give thanks for this bounty by praying to your Lord alone, not associating anything with Him, and likewise with sacrifice, so do not slaughter for other than Him, the Most High. In this there is instruction for his Ummah. Whether the intended prayer is the prayer of the Eid and the sacrifice is the udhiyah (sacrificial animal) is not a barrier to this being included within all prayers and acts of worship.

And the words of the Most High, ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾: that is, indeed, your hater at every time and place is the most lowly, the most humiliated, the one cut off in offspring and lineage.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Explanation of Allah the Most High's honouring of His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ).

2- Confirmation of the hadiths about al-Kawthar, and that it is a river in Paradise.

3- The obligation of sincerity in all acts of worship, especially prayer and sacrifice.

4- The legitimacy of invoking curses upon the wrongdoer.
